newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria to set up commodity exchange this year.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria to set up commodity exchange this year.

text.p: Nigeria's commerce minister Rear Admiral Jibril Ayinla said on Monday the African nation would set up a commodity exchange (COMEX) in 1997.
Ayinla, briefing journalists and business executives on this year's fiscal budget, said the exchange would help to stimulate agricultural production in the country as well as exports.
"If we do not export then we shall certainly perish," he said.
His finance ministry counterpart Anthony Ani said the decree establishing the COMEX had already been signed and it would certainly take off this year.
Nigeria has been talking about establishing the COMEX since the early 1990s but has been slow putting together the decree.
Ayinla said the exchange would help to formalise some of the unrecorded trade in Nigerian commodities.
"A lot of goods go out but we will like to see it done formally," he said.
He said an all-African trade fair would be held in the northern Nigerian city of Kaduna between March and April where the idea of the COMEX would also be promoted.
